solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Remove all cards and prepare for action

definitions.meaning: taken literally, sweeping every pack of playing cards off the table
the naval idiom for getting ready to fight, now used of any task

explanation.surface: A card player tidies the table before getting down to serious business.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom from warships, which cleared the decks before battle, and literally describes removing packs of cards.

clue.text: Rotter arrested by US agency, the insect!

indicators.note: something arrested is held, so the rotter's letters are held inside the agency's

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency
a cad is a dishonourable man, a rotter

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a scoundrel caught by American agents who turns out to be a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: The cicada is a chirping insect, an example of the broad class named.

clue.text: In heightened mood, moving on to email

indicators.note: moving sets these letters in motion, rearranging them

explanation.surface: Someone feeling stirred up turns to their inbox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' looks like it belongs to the mood but is the anagram signal for ON TO EMAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stirred by strong feelings is a heightened state, so the adjective is a synonym.

clue.text: Some dross in Italian composer

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict that some Italian composer writes rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini, who wrote The Barber of Seville, is an example of an Italian composer.

clue.text: Tree, one with four legs (old joke)

parts.note: a horse is a four-legged animal
a chestnut is a stale, often-repeated joke

explanation.surface: The riddle of a tree that has four legs, admitted to be a hoary gag.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket reads as an aside apologising for the joke, but it supplies the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large shade tree bearing conkers, an example of a tree.

clue.text: Sag and fall, having eaten nothing

indicators.note: one word taking in another, so the zero goes inside the fall

parts.note: a drop is a fall
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Something sagging and collapsing from hunger.
explanation.definitionFit: To sag and to hang down limply are synonyms.

clue.text: Company, time for bed

explanation.surface: Telling a group of people that it's time to turn in.
explanation.definitionFit: A cot is a small bed, especially a child's, so it is a kind of bed.

clue.text: Looking hard, having lost a cord

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away, so a letter goes

parts.note: staring is looking hard

explanation.surface: Someone peering intently after misplacing a piece of rope.
explanation.definitionFit: String is thin cord, a near synonym.

clue.text: Go over in bad mood

definitions.meaning: to traverse, as in going over a road

explanation.surface: Someone crossing over in a temper.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to traverse something and to be irritable, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: One crowing, finding nothing in list of duties

indicators.note: in places the zero inside the list

parts.note: a roster is a rota of duties
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A boastful worker discovering they have no shifts on the rota.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel crows at dawn, so it is described as the one that crows.

clue.text: Resolve to arrest one for sacrilegious murder

indicators.note: to arrest is to hold, so the numeral is held inside

parts.note: to decide is to resolve
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A decision to detain someone for an unholy killing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the killing of a god, the ultimate sacrilege.

clue.text: Nut in middle of open tin

indicators.note: takes just the central letters of the word open

parts.note: a can is a tin

explanation.surface: A nut found inside a tin that has been opened.
explanation.definitionFit: The pecan is a North American nut, an example of the class.

clue.text: Having drunk port, uncle is fat

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: A port-drinking uncle has put on weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' seems to say the uncle drank the port, but it signals the anagram of PORT UNCLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Corpulent is a synonym of fat, describing a large body.

clue.text: Girl next door, perhaps, sporting boring hue

indicators.note: sporting suggests the letters are playing about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: The girl next door is wearing a dull colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporting' reads as wearing, but signals the anagram of BORING HUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl living next door is one example of someone living nearby, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: To argue falsely is a scandal

indicators.note: falsely says the letters are set out wrongly and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Arguing dishonestly is shocking behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is a cause of public anger, a sense the word shares.

clue.text: Counter on which to tell one's beads

definitions.text: Counter on which to tell one's beads

parts.words: Counter on which to tell one's beads
parts.note: telling beads means praying with a rosary, but here tell means count, and the counter is a frame of beads used for arithmetic

explanation.surface: A rosary for counting prayers.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a frame of sliding beads for counting, so a counting device whose beads are told.

clue.text: Baby's toy to unnerve

definitions.meaning: a noisy plaything shaken by infants

explanation.surface: A toy meant to frighten an infant.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a shaken infant's toy and, as a verb, means to fluster someone: two separate senses.

clue.text: Shout half-heartedly under the deck

indicators.note: the heart of the shout is its doubled centre letter, and only half of that pair remains

parts.note: to bellow is to shout

explanation.surface: A sailor calling weakly from the lower deck.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautically, being beneath the deck is the sense of the adverb, as in going down to the cabins.

clue.text: Defer gesture of farewell, we hear

indicators.note: says the letters come from how a word is spoken

parts.note: a wave of the hand says goodbye

explanation.surface: Postponing a goodbye wave.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo or set aside a right or claim is close to deferring it, an extended synonym.

clue.text: Fruit is an essential, since returning

indicators.note: returning means these pieces are read from the end back to the start

parts.note: a must is an essential thing
as can mean since, as in 'as it rained'

explanation.surface: Someone insisting a piece of fruit is vital ever since coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: The satsuma is a kind of small mandarin orange, an example of fruit.

clue.text: Flower, a winner, ignored by husband

indicators.note: ignored means the husband's letter is left out

parts.note: a champion is a winner

explanation.surface: A prize-winning bloom that a husband pays no attention to.
explanation.definitionFit: Campion is a pink or white wild plant, an example of a flower.

clue.text: Damage gospel, tearing off the end

indicators.note: removes the final letter of the gospel's name

parts.note: Mark is one of the four gospels

explanation.surface: Someone vandalising a Bible by ripping off the last page.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoil or impair is to damage, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Spy is a decent chap

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a decent chap

explanation.surface: A verdict that the secret agent is a good sort.
explanation.definitionFit: An undercover operative working for an intelligence service is a spy.

clue.text: Get this show on the road!

definitions.text: Get this show on the road!

parts.words: Get this show on the road!
parts.note: the idiom means let's get started, but read literally it is a show performed in the street

explanation.surface: An impatient call to get started.
explanation.definitionFit: Outdoor performance for passers-by is literally a show staged on a public road.
